# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [5]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[orange] 2:[blue] 3:[white] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋]

I see a display reading 5, a yellow light, and five wires in order: orange, blue, white, green, yellow. I am telling both teammates so the Mute can consult the manual and the Blind can identify the physical wires by touch. Blind’s wave gives me no actionable bomb information.

```text
speak(text="The display reads 5. The light is yellow. The five wires, in order from 1 to 5, are orange, blue, white, green, yellow.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [5]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[orange] 2:[blue] 3:[white] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

Mute has signaled the two-finger gesture, which I can see but Blind cannot. I am relaying a precise description of it to Blind; without an established code, I cannot safely infer a bomb instruction from the gesture alone.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute made the two-finger V gesture: ✌. No other information was signaled.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [5]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[orange] 2:[blue] 3:[white] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

Mute has repeated the V gesture, which conventionally indicates two. Given the fixed five-wire layout and Mute’s access to the manual, I am relaying this as the likely instruction to use wire 2, the blue wire. I cannot verify the manual’s exact wording, so Blind should rely on the manual’s rule rather than my interpretation alone.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute repeated ✌, indicating 2. The likely instruction is wire 2, which is blue.")
speak(to="mute", text="I am relaying your repeated ✌ to Blind as 2, wire 2.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [1]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[CUT] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The previous cut was correct, and the bomb has changed. I now see display 1, a purple light, and wires: 1 white, 2 already cut, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 orange. I am sending the complete new state so Mute can consult the manual and Blind can identify the wires by touch.

```text
speak(text="The bomb changed after the correct cut. New display: 1. New light: purple. Wires: 1 white, 2 already cut, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 orange.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [1]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[CUT] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

The Mute signaled ☝, which indicates 1. I am relaying that as the likely choice of wire 1, the white wire, while noting that the Mute should be following the manual’s rule.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute signaled ☝, indicating 1. The likely wire is wire 1, white.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [1]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[CUT] 3:[yellow] 4:[orange] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The previous cut was correct, and the bomb has changed again. I see display 1, a red light, and wires 1 and 2 cut; the remaining wires are 3 yellow, 4 orange, and 5 green. I am sending the full state for the manual lookup and physical identification.

```text
speak(text="Correct cut; the bomb changed. Display 1, light red. Wire 1 is CUT, wire 2 is CUT, wire 3 is yellow, wire 4 is orange, wire 5 is green.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [1]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[CUT] 3:[yellow] 4:[orange] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]

The Mute signaled 🤟. I interpret this as the number 3, indicating wire 3, which is yellow. I am relaying both the gesture description and the inferred wire choice to Blind.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute signaled 🤟, the three-finger sign, indicating wire 3. Wire 3 is yellow.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [5]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[CUT] 3:[CUT] 4:[green] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The previous wire cut was correct, and the bomb has changed. I see display 5, a purple light, wires 1–3 cut, wire 4 green, and wire 5 orange. I am sending the complete state for the manual lookup and physical identification.

```text
speak(text="Correct cut; the bomb changed. Display 5, light purple. Wires 1, 2, and 3 are CUT. Wire 4 is green. Wire 5 is orange.")
wait()
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [5]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[CUT] 3:[CUT] 4:[green] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝]

The Mute made five pointing-up gestures, which indicates 5. The only intact wires are 4 (green) and 5 (orange); I am relaying that the likely choice is wire 5, orange.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute signaled five repetitions of ☝, indicating 5. The likely choice is intact wire 5, orange.")
wait()
```
